title: One Point Lesson - Compressor Suction/Discharge Valve Inspection (OPL-KC-4501-02)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-KC-4501-02 - Compressor Suction/Discharge Valve Inspection.

Equipment: KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR), Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 4500 - RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: SEQ-4501 (SIL 2), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-4501.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains compressor suction/discharge valve inspection for KC-4501 (RECYCLE GAS COMPRESSOR) in the RECYCLE GAS SYSTEM. Broken plate valves are the classic cause of high discharge temperature (TSHH-4503) and lost capacity on KC-4501. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Isolate, depressurise and purge the cylinder with nitrogen
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Remove the suction and discharge valve caps
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Inspect valve plates, springs and seats; replace as a complete set
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Check the valve gasket and seat for damage
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Torque the valve caps to spec and leak test before start
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: High discharge temperature trip TSHH-4503, capacity drop | Likely Cause: 1st stage suction plate valve fractured | Action: Replaced complete suction valve set, checked seat, leak tested
- Symptom: KC-4501 tripped on PSLL-4504 low lube oil pressure | Likely Cause: Lube oil pump gears worn, relief valve set low | Action: Overhauled lube oil pump, reset relief valve, verified 2.5 barg
- Symptom: High blow-by, low 2nd stage efficiency | Likely Cause: PTFE piston rings worn beyond limit | Action: Renewed 2nd stage PTFE piston and rider rings, honed cylinder

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Broken plate valves are the classic cause of high discharge temperature (TSHH-4503) and lost capacity on KC-4501.
- Point 2: Respect the interlock SEQ-4501: e.g. PSLL-4504 trips at < 1.5 barg - never defeat it without a permit.
- Point 3: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-4501 before working on KC-4501.
- Point 4: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
